newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Savage says 1st half down on year ago.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Savage says 1st half down on year ago.

text.p: Zinc and coal miner Savage Resources Ltd said on Friday that its profit for the first half is currently esimated to be about A$5 million below the previous corresponding half year's result.

"The profit for the first half is currently estimated to be about A$5 million below the corresponding half year's results," Savage chairman Richard Austen said in a copy of his speech to be delivered to the annual general meeting.
"Although there is some optimism that the zinc price may be improving, for the time being our cautionary approach remains unchanged," he said.
Each U.S. one per pound move in the international zinc price means A$2.2 million to Savage's bottom line.
Austen told shareholders the company's zinc mining and refining business in Tennessee achieved record production levels of both intermediate concentrates and metal.

"Not withstanding an average London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc price for the year of (U.S.) one cent below the LME zinc price for the prior year, strong germanium byproduct revenue underpinned the zinc profit of A$20 million," Austen said.
He also said that the company's Liddell coal operation in the Hunter Valley performed above forecast during the year.
"The production rate is now in excess of 2.2 million tonnes per annum," Austen said.
Investment in grass roots exploration over the last 18 months would enable Savage to undertake major drilling programs on target sites in Peru, West Kentucky and Western Australia, Austen said.
In July, Savage reported a net profit of A$23.1 million for the year to June 30, 1996, up A$14.9 million from the previous years earnings of A$8.2 million.
